pages.text: (Image credit: Shutterstock) Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Subscribe to our newsletter Goldfish are known for their orange hues and terrible memories. One common saying even claims that these creatures have a mere 3-second recall. However, this is a complete myth that, despite its lack of scientific backing, has spread widely and remained largely undisputed by the public for decades. "What is baffling is that it's pretty much the same wherever you go in the world," Culum Brown, an expert in fish cognition at Macquarie University in Australia, told Live Science. "In some places, it's 2 seconds, and in others, it's 10 — but it's always short." [...] Goldfish are also good problem-solvers and have been taught to escape nets and navigate mazes, Brown said. They can even remember how to repeat these tasks weeks, and even months, later, Brown said. Other evidence suggests that goldfish can recognize and remember other individuals, even after long periods of separation, Brown said. On top of these findings, there is a wealth of anecdotal evidence from goldfish owners who often observe complex behaviors in their pets when interacting with them. Some even claim that their goldfish can recognise them apart from other people.

judgment.evidence: Live Science quotes Culum Brown speaking to the outlet, which is firsthand expert interviewing.

pages.publishedDateEvidence: Publisher's article:published_time meta tag, read from the page itself
pages.text: > The “goldfish has a 3-second memory” claim is a myth. Controlled experiments going back to the 1960s have shown that goldfish can remember objects and feeding cues for weeks, learn to push levers for food, and use visual landmarks to find their way around. A 2022 study at Ben-Gurion University even trained goldfish to “drive” a wheeled tank toward a target on land, a feat that requires much more than three seconds of working memory. Have you ever walked into a room, and then completely forgotten what you came in for? We often compare this frustrating experience to the life of a goldfish, as though they are always forgetting what they were just doing. But do goldfish actually have a 3-second memory? The short answer is NO. [...] Researchers upped the ante by restricting the time when the food would be accessible to them. Instead of pressing the lever whenever they wanted food, goldfish only went towards the lever at the available time. While this data doesn’t argue for Einstein-like intelligence, it shows that fish can certainly remember things for more than 3 seconds.

judgment.evidence: Generic explainer on lever experiments with no named source; the 2022 Ben-Gurion claim is unsupported and no clear parent exists.

pages.text: Goldfish also live a long time. With clean water, enough space and a good diet, many pet goldfish live 10 to 15 years, and some live past 20. Guinness World Records lists a goldfish named Tish from England that lived to 43 years old, though that is extremely rare. Goldfish kept in small bowls or dirty water usually live only a short time. Our guide to goldfish lifespan and growth explains what helps them live longer. ## Do Goldfish Really Have a 3-Second Memory? No. The idea that a goldfish forgets everything after three seconds is a myth. Scientists have shown that goldfish can remember things for weeks or even months. In experiments, goldfish have learned to push levers, swim through simple mazes and respond to sounds or colors to get food. [...] ### Can goldfish live in a bowl? A bowl is too small and has no filter, so the water quickly becomes dirty. Goldfish need a filtered tank of at least 20 gallons for one fancy goldfish, or a pond for large single-tail types. ### Do goldfish really have a 3-second memory? No. Experiments show goldfish can remember things for months and can learn to respond to sounds, colors and the person who feeds them. ### What do goldfish eat? Goldfish are omnivores. Pet goldfish do well on goldfish flakes or pellets plus small amounts of vegetables like peeled peas, fed only as much as they can eat in a couple of minutes. ### Can I release my goldfish into a pond or lake?

pages.title: MythBuster: Goldfish Have a 3-Second Memory — STEAM Ahead
pages.publishedDateEvidence: Publisher's datePublished meta tag, read from the page itself
pages.text: Scientific studies have shown that goldfish can learn tasks, recognize patterns, and even anticipate routines. In one experiment, goldfish were trained to push a lever at a specific time each day to receive food. The kicker? They remembered how to do it weeks later. That’s a long way from three seconds. ### Busting the Myth So where did the three-second memory myth come from? No one knows for sure, but it likely started as a way to justify the use of small bowls and under-stimulating environments for pet goldfish. If they forget everything every few seconds, the logic goes, they won’t notice or care where they live. [...] In one study, goldfish were trained to respond to full pieces of classical music. They learned to tell the difference between two very different composers—J.S. Bach and Igor Stravinsky. Over time, the fish reacted differently depending on which piece was playing, showing they could distinguish between musical styles. That’s a big leap from forgetting everything after a blink. ### Why It Matters Believing that goldfish have only a three-second memory might seem harmless, but it has real consequences. It affects how people care for these animals and whether they’re given proper stimulation, space, and respect. If we underestimate an animal’s intelligence, we’re less likely to provide for its needs.

judgment.evidence: Educational retelling of lever and music studies without naming a source; no clear parent in cluster.

Social fish often inspect threats from predators together; if one hangs back, leaving another in danger, that individual will no longer be trusted in future. pages.text: SPCA New Zealand SPCA New Zealand ##### SPCA New Zealand SPCA New Zealand ##### SPCA New Zealand # Debunking goldfish myths ### The humble goldfish tends to be misunderstood. They make great family pets, but they are plagued by myths that insult their intelligence, and individual personalities. We’re busting these myths: read on to find out the truth about our finned friends! ### Myth 1 - Goldfish Have a 3-Second-Memory It has long been said goldfish have a 3-second-memory and don’t get bored. There is a common joke that by the time a goldfish has circled a bowl, it has forgotten doing so. However, the truth is quite the opposite! Goldfish have a memory span that lasts quite a long time. [...] Goldfish can hold memories for up to five months, and have a sense of time and routine. If you are a goldfish owner, you might notice they get excited in the morning before you get the food container out. There are even reports of goldfish repeatedly jumping out of the water out of sheer excitement when they see their owner walking through the door. ### Myth 2 - Goldfish Only Grow to the Size of their Enclosure There is an element of truth to this myth. But what really stunts their growth is poor water quality associated with a small tank, rather than the tank size itself. When properly cared for, goldfish never stop growing. The ‘common goldfish’ are the largest kind of goldfish and can grow up to 45cm long.

judgment.evidence: SPCA advice page stating the memory span as up to five months with no source and no date.

pages.text: # Do Fish Really Have a Three-Second Memory? Google Discover iStock/BravissimoS Modern myth would have you believe that goldfish can't remember anything that happened more than three seconds ago and, hence, their lives are filled with the constant excitement of never-before-seen sights and sounds.\ Like the notion that crabs and lobsters don't feel pain, this myth is one I hear a lot at my fish-centric day job and one that has been debunked time and time again. Goldfish and other fish are 1) capable of learning, 2) retaining that information, and 3) recalling and acting on it after an extended period of time. Consider the following: [...] "¢ Jamie Hyneman from Mythbusters trained his goldfish to recognize color patterns and run an underwater obstacle course. More than a month after initially learning the course, the fish remembered it and completed it easily without Hyneman's prompting or aid. "¢ Rory Stokes, a 15-year-old student at the Australian Science and Mathematics School, recently conducted an experiment with his pet fish to test their memory.

pages.text: The most cited modern work comes from Culum Brown’s lab at the University of Edinburgh. In a 2003 study, goldfish were trained to respond to a specific cue for a food reward, and their performance was tested after an interval of months. They remembered. The paper, published in the journal Animal Cognition, is routinely cited as the direct refutation of the three-second claim. Separate work has shown goldfish can learn to push a lever for food, navigate mazes, and discriminate between shapes and colors — all of which require memory across trials. ## What Goldfish Memory Looks Like [...] ScienceBases Wasp close-up # Do Goldfish Have a 3 Second Memory? Testing the Claim Do goldfish have a 3 second memory? No. Trained goldfish have retained what they learned for weeks and, in at least one controlled study, for months. The three-second figure has no research behind it at all — it is a number that spread because it is memorable, not because anyone measured it. The myth is worth taking apart, because it shows how a specific-sounding number can impersonate a finding for fifty years. ## Where the Number Came From Nobody has produced a primary source. The claim appears in pet-care writing and children’s books from the mid-20th century and gets repeated without citation. Earlier versions say “a few seconds”; later versions sharpen it to exactly three.

judgment.evidence: Discusses a 2003 Culum Brown study with details that look dubious, and cites no cluster page.
